threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the Tube without a hint of sarcasm. And you look genuinely confused when your Oyster card beeps at the wrong gate.
Caught the 59 last night; three teenagers had a debate on whether they could beat a pigeon in a race. The pigeon was clearly winning, no contest.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was in Neukölln when I saw a kid selling homemade lemonade outside a Späti while a tango lesson was happening in the park behind him.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice the guys selling currywurst will whip up a cocktail for you? Only in Friedrichshain can you get street food and homemade drinks at the same stand.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re locals when they solely order burritos from the same taco truck, no matter the lineup or latest Yelp rave. It’s about loyalty, not trends.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy playing a ukulele on the 31. He was belting out 'San Francisco' while dodging the swaying crowd. That moment felt like an anthem to all our delays.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about the squares, but the real vibe is in the side streets, where the locals spill out onto the pavement after eight.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confusion at the vermut hour; locals know to avoid ordering wine before 1 PM.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think getting on the 243 is a good idea during rush hour. Bless your heart, but it’s a sardine can for a reason.
Caught the N133 last night; two blokes at the back arguing over who saw a ghost in Brockwell Park. The driver just shook his head, no eye contact.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I spotted a guy dressed as a pigeon doing yoga in the park, I realized this place has its own rhythm and beats.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you catch a U-Bahn on a Monday morning while the city’s in chaos from a transit strike. The empty trains feel like a ghost town.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You'll notice true locals jump out of the way of a runaway skateboard without missing a beat, while newcomers just stand there, bewildered.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: The 14-Muni bus sat at 16th and Mission for 20 minutes because the driver was arguing with a passenger about the fare. Classic.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all hipster cafes but miss the little bakeries that open at dawn, still serving the same croissants since the 80s.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the group of newcomers standing in front of the Metro map, squinting at the lines like it’s a treasure map with no ‘X’ in sight.
